text.p: The Coca-Cola Co. said Tuesday it was on track to meet its target of increasing worldwide unit case sales by 7 percent to 8 percent and earnings per share growth in the upper teens to 20 percent for 1996.
"We expect to meet or slightly exceed the upper end of that volume growth target in 1996," the company quoted James Chestnut, chief financial officer, as telling a meeting of financial analysts.

Chestnut said Coca-Cola expected third-quarter worldwide volume growth of 6 percent to 7 percent and that earnings per share would meet consensus analyst estimates before unusual items. The company said the previously-announced one-time items would improve its third-quarter earnings slightly.
Analysts expect Coca-Cola to report earnings per share of 38 cents in the third quarter, up from 32 cents in the year-ago period.

The company's profits rose to $1.05 billion, or 42 cents a share, in the second quarter, from $898 million, or 35 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew to $5.3 billion from $4.9 billion.

Coca-Cola also said it was reducing concentrate inventory levels held by some bottlers to strengthen its worldwide bottler system. Concentrate gallon sales in the quarter would be about even with sales in the same period last year, it said.
The reduction would result in a one-time after-tax charge of $180 million to $200 million in the third quarter, it said.
The company also said it would record a $60 million after-tax provision to launch a programme to redesign its information systems and communications capabilities.

Coca-Cola also said it has taken various provisions totalling about $180 million to $200 million after-tax for structural changes at different divisions. The provisions will be recorded in the third quarter.
Structural changes would occur primarily in Greater Europe, Latin America and North America, mainly at Coca-Cola Foods, it said.
Coca-Cola's stock fell $1.25 to $49.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
